note: A3.1 x A3.4 interaction guard. A3.1 makes the route index treat the method string "ANY" as a wildcard, so an ANY route pairs with any client verb. Dart's go_router emits every GoRoute with method "ANY" — so without A3.4's nav marking, turning on the ANY tier would make EVERY go_router entry an HTTP_CALLS target and this same-app `dio.get('/users')` would pair to the app's own navigation table. A3.4 stamps those ROUTEs with an ORIGIN `provenance: nav_route` cell and build_route_index skips them. Deliberately legacy-only (no `cells`): dart/http_client is already measured by dart-http-dio, this is its precision twin. Both nodes must survive — only the pairing must never exist. LB.4c: go_router entries are `page:<path>` (name = the path; ROUTE_METHOD ANY kept), so a page never shares an identity with a server `ANY /users`; the forbid row targets the page's qname.

expect_nodes.name: page:/users
expect_nodes.note: go_router nav route (LB.4c: qname `page:/users`) — still a node ('where is /users rendered?' is a real query), just never an HTTP target

expect_nodes.name: endpoint:GET:/users
expect_nodes.note: the same-app dio.get, an outbound call to a REMOTE server

forbid.note: THE INTERACTION BUG: an ANY-method browser navigation target is not a server endpoint. Matched EXACTLY on the endpoint's qname and the nav page's qname `page:/users` (LB.4c).
